translations.answer: The operable part of the original post involves replaying multi-season sensor data on the same route and synchronizing checks with LiDAR, radar, camera, and IMU. A fix is not provided. The seasonal offset should be treated as an independent test dimension and not limited to single-season calibration.
translations.applicability: Suitable for long-term deployment state estimation regression testing.
translations.credibility.rationale: The solution has not closed or there is a conflict; the current state is only forming a problem clue.
translations.details.attempts.0: Published multi-season sensor data and FiftyOne multi-modal replay.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Used GNSS ground truth to align multi-sensor MCAP replays and cross-season comparison.
translations.details.environments.0: Quebec forest; 12 deployments; -19°C to 18°C; about 1 m of snow.
translations.details.limits.0: Not human-like; 4%/46% definition and algorithm configuration require data card.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Quantified seasonal offset, but no fix algorithm is provided.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Same-locator positioning algorithm shows severe drift after seasonal change.
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Position drift should be controlled; if not, reduce autonomous speed and use independent true value/invalid detection to limit WBC navigation commands.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Snow changes road geometry and LiDAR appearance, leading to long-term scene inconsistency.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Drift on the same route increases from 4% to 46%.
translations.media_summaries.0: Screenshot repeats drift 4%→46% and sensor/temperature range, without trajectory or error definition.
translations.source.title: Seasonal change causes LiDAR-inertial SLAM drift from 4% to 46%
